argument: Recomputation kills the headline of f-001 and the collapsing arithmetic of f-003, and leaves only a source objection standing. Anchored to the defender's own play band, a Master-tier defender reads 9/15/21 whose Weak value is 9: subtracting 7 leaves 2/8/14 and the shipped 8 leaves 1/7/13, three separable tiers in both cases, so the plate's size sits inside the invariant, and the shipped ladder 2/5/8 fits its three band Weak values 2/6/9 exactly, which is the fingerprint of a defender-band anchor. Anchored instead to whatever an opponent swings, the same test convicts canon: the shipped Master rung at 8 against a Challenge 3 knight's middle row yields 1/1/4, a worse collapse than the plate's 1/2/5 at 7, so a premise that indicts shipped canon is the wrong premise. The surviving core of f-001 is the source rule alone, that a worn card may not supply a hero's reduction; its invariant breach does not survive. f-003's 1/1/2 fails the same way: a bare 2-point reduction on the Novice row floors 2 to 1, turns 4 into 2 and 6 into 4, still three distinct values, which the armour chapter's own worked example demonstrates. The identical collapse needs a Shield Block step-down underneath the subtraction, and a Novice rung plus an ordinary shield, with no magic item present, reproduces 1/1/2 exactly, so that arithmetic indicts the stacking, not the item. My tests confirm rather than break f-004 (tested rarity, slot, passive, power: the Shroud is a superset at equal cost under every reading) and the core of f-007 (4 per level against a cap of 2 after unit conversion), and reduce f-005 to a compressed recap plus a self-explaining consumable exception. The reading that survives the attack: the invariant is anchored to the defender's play band.

evidence.claim: The only shipped heroic reduction ladder is 2 at Novice, 5 at Adept and 8 at Master, and it is carried by a talent card rather than by anything a hero wears.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: *Novice:* You have DR 2. ... *Master:* You have DR 8.

evidence.claim: Band-anchored recomputation: on the defender's own tier the top row 9/15/21 has Weak value 9, so 7 subtraction gives 2/8/14 and the shipped 8 gives 1/7/13, both sets three separable values. Reading the subtraction against 6/9/12 instead gives 1/1/4 at 8 and 1/2/5 at 7.

The shipped ladder 2 then 5 then 8 sits at or just under the Weak value of its own band (2, 6, 9), which is exactly the tuning a defender-band anchor predicts and cannot be explained by an attacker-row anchor.

Indictment test: the attacker-row reading convicts shipped canon harder than it convicts the plate, because 8 against the middle row merges two outcome values where 7 leaves them apart. A premise that damns canon is not fit to damn an item, so f-001's invariant breach falls and only its source objection remains.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: DR 8 vs knight 6/9/12 gives 1/1/4; DR 7 gives 1/2/5

evidence.claim: The armour chapter routes a hero's subtraction through training, says worn armour supplies none of it, and keeps a landed hit at a floor of one point.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Your DR comes from talents such as Iron Skin

evidence.claim: At the levels the Very Rare entry is placed for, opponents still swing the middle row: a Challenge 3 knight attacks there and a Challenge 6 caster mixes its rows.

Reproduced f-003's spread: the shield reaction alone separates 2/4/6 into 1/2/4, and stacking a 2-point subtraction on top merges the two lowest into 1/1/2. The arithmetic is right, the attribution is not.
The shield's own reaction is a one-step downgrade, and its worked example runs a bare 2-point reduction on the Novice row and still reads three distinct results.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Reduce the damage tier by one step

evidence.claim: That same chapter's worked fight shows the weak hit flooring at one, the standard hit landing at two, and the strong hit at four under a bare 2-point reduction, which is the three-value spread itself.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: DR 2 soaks 2, so Roric takes 2 damage

evidence.claim: Counter-example: a hero on the Novice rung with the ordinary shield's block and no magic item anywhere reproduces 1/1/2 identically, and that rung is legal at level one. So the collapse belongs to the stacking of a downgrade with any 2-point subtraction, not to this item.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Novice DR 2 + ordinary shield block: 1/1/2, no item

evidence.claim: The combat chapter grants a shield Parry and the block reaction and no bonus of its own, and it halves resistant damage with rounding down while never fixing the order against a flat subtraction, so the ordering gap f-001 raises is a combat-chapter omission that every reduction-plus-resistance entry shares.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: enables Parry and Shield Block, but never adds a roll bonus

evidence.claim: Both cloaks carry the same rarity, the same attunement cost and the same worn slot; one Stealth Boon is gated to a terrain type while the other carries no qualifier and adds a once-per-encounter repositioning power.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: While in natural surroundings ... Boon on Stealth checks

evidence.claim: Tested f-004 strictly on the enumerated capabilities: rarity equal, attunement equal, slot equal, passive a superset, plus an extra power on one side. No counter-example found, so domination holds; it does not depend on the reading, because even if the terrain gate costs nothing the extra power still decides it.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: rarity =, slot =, passive superset, power +1 => dominated

evidence.claim: The entry guide's activation rule carries the hero's attribute and the matching skill; the catalog's recap keeps only the attribute, an omission rather than a contrary rule, and the vial's line explains that its own magic rather than the user sets the outcome.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: no modifiers, the potion's magic, not your skill

evidence.claim: The potion still rolls one 3d6 and reads one outcome row, which is the one-roll law satisfied, and it is a consumable whose power is not the user's, a narrow exception its own text declares. So :28 and :42 are one rule at two levels of detail and :442 adds an explained exception rather than a third rule.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 3d6, one tier, one row => :28 and :42 agree

evidence.claim: The middle band of the closing note grants each individual hero two uncommon items and one rare item inside a three-level window, while the top band pools its rarest item for the whole party, so the note changes unit partway down.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Two Uncommon, one Rare per hero.

evidence.claim: The GM chapter is where item flow is defined: one or two items per level for a whole party, the per-character unit ruled out, permanents kept significant and consumables the generous hand-out.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 1–2 per level, per party. Not per character

evidence.claim: Unit conversion confirms f-007's core: three permanents per hero across three levels becomes twelve for a four-hero party, four per level, against a cap of two for the whole party, and the gap widens because the cap counts consumables while the band counts permanents only.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 12 permanents / 3 levels = 4 per level vs cap 2

evidence.claim: One clause of f-007 does not survive: the opening band's four hero items plus the party's named one already reach the canonical level-three total once its consumables are counted, so the middle band is not uniquely the outlier, though the unit flip between the first two bands and the third still stands.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: band one: 5 permanents + potions >= 3-6 at level 3
